name: sagebrush-mcp

tools.name: sage
tools.description: Run Sage code in a persistent Sagebrush session (variables persist between calls). Sage syntax: 2^10 is a power, 1/3 is exact, R.<x> = QQ[] defines a polynomial ring, [1..10] is a range. Number theory (factoring, number fields, class groups, units), polynomials, exact matrices over ZZ/QQ, modular forms and newforms, elliptic curves, symbolic calculus (diff, integrate, limit, solve, desolve), 2D and 3D plots (returned as SVG). Returns the printed output and the value of the last line. Call `guide` for the list of what is implemented.

timeout.description: seconds before the computation is interrupted (default 60, at most 3600)

tools.name: python
tools.description: Run plain Python (no Sage preparsing) in the same persistent session; the Sage names (from sagebrush.sage import *) and the engine modules (sagebrush.nf, .linalg, .poly, .mf, .modsym, .ap) are available.

timeout.description: seconds before the computation is interrupted (default 60, at most 3600)

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the documentation of Sagebrush's Sage library: every public function and method with its signature, summary and docstring (tested examples; OPEN PROBLEM sections mark open problems). Every word of the query must match; matches in the name rank first. Use it to find what Sagebrush can do; in the sage tool, name? shows one function's full documentation.

query.description: words to look for, e.g. "elliptic rank", "class group", "galois"

full.description: include each result's whole docstring (default false)

tools.name: reset
tools.description: Restart the session: all variables are cleared.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: What Sagebrush implements (Sage functions and objects), with examples.

tools.name: factor
tools.description: Factor an integer (ECM; any size that ECM can split), e.g. n = "2^128 + 1".

n.description: an integer or an integer expression

tools.name: number_field
tools.description: Invariants of the number field Q[x]/(f): degree, signature, discriminant, integral basis, class group, class number, regulator, unit rank and torsion (class group and units assume GRH).

polynomial.description: an irreducible polynomial in x, e.g. "x^3 - 11"

tools.name: newforms
tools.description: The Galois orbits of newforms of level N and weight k (trivial character): LMFDB labels, dimensions, q-expansions and Hecke characteristic polynomials.

instructions:
Sagebrush is free (MIT/Apache) computational mathematics: number theory,
algebra and exact linear algebra, with a Sage-compatible interface, run by
fast Rust engines. Use the `sage` tool for anything (Sage syntax: 2^10,
R.<x> = QQ[], 1/3 is exact); variables persist between calls. Call `guide`
for what is implemented. Results are exact; class groups and units assume
GRH where Sage/PARI do.
